chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ja'far: 'O Ja'far! Shall I confer upon you? Shall I give you? Shall I gift you?' So Ja'far said to him: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'So the people thought that he would give him gold or silver, and the people anticipated for that.'

So he said to him: 'I am giving you something, if you were to act upon it every day, it would be better for you than the world and whatever is in it, and if you were to do it in between two days, Allah would forgive you whatever is between them, or every Friday, or every month, or every year, He would forgive you whatever is between them.'

You should pray four Rak'at. You begin by reciting and saying, when you are finished: 'Glory be to Allah, and the Praise is for Allah, and there is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.' You say that fifteen times after the recitation.

So when you bow, say it ten times. So when you raise your head from the bowing, say it ten times. So when you prostrate, say it ten times. So when you raise your head from the prostration, say it ten times between the two prostrations.
So when you perform the second prostration, say it ten times. So when you raise your head from the second prostration, say it ten times, while you are seated, before you stand.

So that is seventy-five glorifications in every Rak'at, three hundred glorifications in four Rak'at. In four (Rak'at) there are one thousand two hundred glorifications, and extollations of Oneness, and exclamations of Takbir, and praises.
If you so desire, pray it during the day, and if you so desire, pray it at night.

And in a report of Ibrahim ibn Abdul Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'You should recite in the first (Rak'at) When the Earth is Shaken, and in the second And the Runners, and in the third When there comes the Help of Allah, and in the fourth Say: He is Allah, One.'

I said, 'So what is its reward?' He said: 'If there were upon him sins like the grains of sand, Allah would forgive them for him.' Then he looked at me and said: 'But rather, that is for you and for your companions.'
ai.seo_question: What is the method and reward of the Prayer of Glorification (Salat al-Tasbih) as narrated in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the spiritual gift of Salat al-Tasbih to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, emphasizing its efficacy for daily, bi-daily, or periodic recitation to secure forgiveness. The narration specifies the exact distribution of the 300 glorifications across the four Rak'at and recommends specific Surahs for each unit, linking the practice to the profound reward of having sins forgiven like the grains of 'Aalj. This prayer is particularly cherished in Shia tradition as a means of maintaining consistent spiritual discipline and divine mercy.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Yahya Al-Halby, from Haroun Bin Jariya, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Ja’far<sup>as</sup> (Bin Abu Talib<sup>as</sup>): ‘O Ja’far<sup>as</sup>!

Shall I<sup>saww</sup> confer upon you<sup>as</sup>, shall I<sup>saww</sup> give you<sup>as</sup>, shall I gift you<sup>as</sup> (something)?’ So Ja’far<sup>as</sup> said to him<sup>saww</sup>: ‘Yes, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So the people thought that he<sup>saww</sup> would give him<sup>as</sup> some gold or silver, and the people anticipated for that.

So he<sup>saww</sup> said to him<sup>asws</sup>: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> am giving you<sup>as</sup> something, if you<sup>as</sup> were to act upon it during every day, it would be better for you<sup>as</sup> than the world and whatever is in it, and if you<sup>as</sup> were to do it in between two days, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive for you<sup>as</sup> whatever (you<sup>as</sup> committed) what is between the two (days), or every Friday, or every month, or every year, (your<sup>as</sup> sins) would be Forgive for you<sup>as</sup> whatever (you<sup>as</sup> committed) between the two.

You<sup>as</sup> should pray four Rak’at. You<sup>as</sup> should begin reciting and you<sup>as</sup> should be saying, when you<sup>as</sup> are free: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest’. You should say that fifteen times after the recitation.

So when youas go down into Rukū say it ten times. So when youas raise youras head from the Rukū, say it ten times. So when youas perform Sajdah, say it ten times. So when youas raise youras head from the Sajdah, say it ten times between the two Sajdahs.
So when youas perform Sajdah the second (Sajdah) say it ten times. So when youas raise youras head from the second Sajdah say it ten times, while youas are seated, before youas stand.

So that would be seventy-five Glorifications during every Rak’at, being three hundred Glorification in four Rak’at. In four (Rak’at) there would be one thousand two hundred Glorifications, and Extollations of Oneness, and exclamations of Takbīr’s, and Praises.
If you<sup>as</sup> so desire to, pray it during the day, and if you<sup>as</sup> so desire to, pray it at night’.

And in a report of Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws (having said): ‘You should recite in the first (Rak’at) [99:1] When the earth is shaken (Chapter 99), and in the second (Rak’at) [100:1] I swear by the runners (Chapter 100), and in the third (Rak’at) [110:1] When there comes the help of Allah (Chapter 110), and in the fourth (Rak’at) [112:1] Say He Allah is One (Chapter 112)’. I said, ‘So what are its Rewards?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there were upon him sin like the grains of sand, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive them for him’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> looked at me, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, that is for you and for your companions (The Shias)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Yahya al-Halabiy from Harun ibn Kharijah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah once said to Ja‘far: ‘O Ja‘far, should I grant you and give an award to you or a gift?’ Ja‘far then said, ‘Yes, O Messenger of Allah, please do so.’ The narrator has said that people thought the Messenger of Allah might give him gold or silver. People remained anticipating.

The Messenger of Allah said, ‘I give you something and if you practice every day, it will be better for you than the whole world and all that it contains. If you practice it every two days, Allah forgives you during the time in between. For your practicing it every Friday or every month or every year, Allah grants you forgiveness during the time in between.

Perform four Rak‘at Salah (prayer). Begin the Salah (prayer), complete the recitations and then say, “Allah is free of all defects, all praise belongs to Allah, no one, other than Allah, deserves worship and Allah is great” fifteen times.

In Ruku‘ position, say it ten times. After Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees)’, when standing, say it ten times. In the first sajdah say it ten times. When sitting between the two sajdah say it ten times.
In the second sajdah say it ten times. After the second sajdah before standing up for the second Rak‘at say it ten times.

This amounts to seventy-five Tasbihah, which makes it three hundred Tasbihah in one Rak‘at and in four Rak‘at Salah (prayer) it becomes one thousand two hundred Tasbihah, Tahlilah, Tahmidah and Takbirah.
You may perform this Salah (prayer) during the day or night as you wish.’

“It is in a Hadith (narration) from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid that abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said the following. ‘In the first Rak‘at after the first Chapter of the Holy Quran recite Chapter 99. In the second Rak‘at you should recite Chapter 100, in the third Rak‘at recite Chapter 110 and in the fourth Rak‘at read Chapter 112 of the Holy Quran.’

I then asked, ‘What is the reward for this Salah (prayer)?’ The Imam replied, ‘If his sins are as many as grains of sand in a pile, Allah forgives him.’ He then looked at me and said, ‘This is for you and your people only.’”
